title: Kalabhra Dynasty
capsule: The Kalabhras were an obscure dynasty that overran much of southern India — displacing the Chola, Pandya, and Chera kingdoms — during what Tamil scholars call the "dark age" between roughly the 3rd and 7th centuries CE. Their origin, language, and capital remain disputed; some inscriptions associate them with Jain or Buddhist patronage, which may explain the hostility of later Brahmanical and devotional Tamil sources that describe them as "evil kings" (kalabhra). They were eventually expelled by the Pallava and Pandya resurgence, with the Pallava king Simhavishnu (r. c. 550–590 CE) and the Pandya Kadungon playing key roles in their displacement. No Kalabhra royal inscription has been definitively identified, making the dynasty one of the most poorly documented ruling houses in Indian history.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is highly uncertain; no contemporary boundary documents survive, and the dynasty's geography is reconstructed from hostile later sources and the areas known to have been disrupted during the period.
